display_name: Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People: every section, with the references and the saving clause of section 4 as typed values

run.method: one agent working alone from the lead's brief (the Israeli defect hunt); tests written by hand from the text before the modules were run

seat: the individual to whom the Basic Law is applied (a resident, a person asked to use or receive a notice in a language, a person asked whether a change to the Basic Law was validly made); no seat for an official

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English. Hebrew from the sources appears only in `-- tag:N |` comments generated by tools/srcquote.py from line N of a deposited source, and in string literals that tools/hebcheck.py checked occur verbatim in a deposited source.

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation; compared word for word with the official page (NOTES.md section 3)

official_source.authority: official publication (the Knesset's PDF of Sefer HaChukim 2743), read from the page image

scope: Every section of the Basic Law (1 to 11): ss 4, 8, 9, 10, 11 as rules; ss 5, 6, 7 as typed State duties; ss 1, 2, 3 as quoted text and typed cross-reference values; the eleven editorial pointers of the consolidation as typed values that are not in the official text. Not encoded: the Declaration on the State Emblem (a drawing), Basic Law: The Knesset (the size of the Knesset is an input), the Hebrew Date Use Law and the other Laws named in the notes beyond what is cited.

expected_red.why: R1, R2: s 2(b) against the Declaration on the State Flag (two colour words). R3: article 82's first sentence names two languages once English is struck; its second sentence still says the three languages.

forks.F1: s 4(c): what a status 'given in practice' reaches. Readings: only a status given in practice; that and a status an enactment gave; declined (default).
forks.F2: s 4(c): the day the Basic Law commenced (no commencement section). Readings: the day it was passed (19 July 2018); the day it was published (26 July 2018); declined (default).
forks.F3: s 4(a): whether 'the language of the State' excludes another language from also being one. Declined: the text is silent (NOTHING).
forks.F4: s 4(b): 'in law' (בחוק) read as the Interpretation Law's 'חוק' (a law of the Knesset or an Ordinance). An Order in Council is not one. Rejected: any enactment, regulations included.
forks.F5: s 11: 'a majority of the members of the Knesset' read as more than half of the members, the number of members an input. Rejected: a majority of those present.
forks.F6: s 9(b): the names printed with a plene yod (הזיכרון) read as the days the Memorial Day Law and the Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day Law name (הזכרון).
forks.F7: s 6(a): 'because of their Jewishness or their citizenship' read as qualifying both groups. Rejected: only the citizens.
forks.F8: s 10: who is a Jew is a fact the person states.
forks.F9: article 82 (cross-referenced instrument): the composite text in the consolidation is CONSOLIDATION-ONLY; only the 1922 page and section 15(b) were read from official images.
forks.F10: The Interpretation Law's encoding was not copied in: its modules use REFUSE, which main does not read; the effect of its ss 3 and 21 is carried as typed values and the text quoted.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source, and no independent tester has run yet. Every expected value was worked by hand from the text before it was asserted. No mutation check was run.

check.note: errors 3 are the 3 declared failed assertions of il40-tests-expected-red.l4; every module has the same four counts on the main build.
